extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in research integrity, mathematical researchers, journal editors, and science journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A news report about the retraction of one mathematician's papers that discusses causes for retraction, editorial investigation practices, peer-review failures, and broader lessons about publication quality and metrics in mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical validity of definitions and results
rubrics_metrics.description: The correctness of the mathematical definitions (e.g., in Section 2), the mathematical validity of stated results (especially key theorems, e.g., Theorem 1), and the correctness of derived consequences and applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction in this case followed an investigation that found errors in definitions, theorems, and physical applications; in mathematics, retractions are commonly made because of erroneous statements. Anti-patterns: publishing papers with incorrect definitions, invalid proofs, or unjustified claims about applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of physical applications / interdisciplinary claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about physical applications or modeling must be supported by correct mathematics and appropriate physical justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article was investigated for the validity of its physical applications (Section 6) and found to contain errors. Authors should not assert physical relevance without appropriate derivation and justification; reviewers should check application claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for outside peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should undergo independent/outside peer review before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One retracted Focus Issue paper was pulled because it never went through an outside peer review. Anti-pattern: accepting or publishing articles (especially in special issues) without sending them to impartial external reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial investigation following COPE guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial investigations into concerns should follow COPE (Committee on Publication Ethics) guidelines and established publisher procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature reported rigorously applying COPE guidelines, consulting its Research Integrity Group, and engaging an independent subject-specific external expert before action. Follow-up actions (correction, retraction) should be based on such procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with independent subject-specific experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess allegations of technical or disciplinary errors by consulting independent, subject-specific external experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher consulted an independent, subject-specific external expert as part of the investigation. Use external experts to evaluate technical validity when editors lack domain expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction to preserve integrity of the scientific record
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction is an appropriate remedy when the scientific validity of results is compromised, to ensure the integrity of the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher concluded that retraction was the most appropriate course to ensure the integrity of the scientific record. Guidance: use retraction when errors invalidate results and cannot be remedied by a correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction of retraction reasons in mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: In mathematics, retractions are typically due to erroneous statements (mathematical errors) rather than data fabrication, image manipulation, or plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters note that retractions in math usually reflect incorrect proofs/statements. This affects how misconduct is characterized and how corrective actions are framed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of editorial correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers often treat correspondence with authors and reviewers as confidential and may withhold editorial-history details for confidentiality reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature stated it cannot comment on editorial history or share investigation details for confidentiality reasons. Guidance: confidentiality can limit transparency, but publishers may cite privacy when refusing to release detailed records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opportunity to correct vs. retract
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may seek to publish corrigenda/corrections, but journals decide if correction is feasible or if retraction is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atangana claimed a corrigendum was to be published, yet the publisher proceeded with retraction; another commenter said he was not given opportunity to correct. Best practice: assess whether errors are fixable via correction and, where appropriate, allow authors to submit corrigenda before retracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence and conflicts in special issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Special issues and guest-editing arrangements must preserve rigorous, independent editorial oversight to avoid conflicts of interest and lowered review standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Focus Issue guest-edited by the author included papers that were later retracted; one was pulled because it never underwent outside peer review. Anti-pattern: guest editors handling papers without impartial external review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to substantive post-publication critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should take substantive post-publication critiques seriously, investigate them, and provide mechanisms (comments, letters, corrections) to correct the literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters documented difficulties getting journals to consider submitted comments; one author eventually had a comment published elsewhere after resubmission. Guidance: timely consideration of well-founded critiques promotes correction of the record; rejecting important corrections without review is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher responsibility to investigate allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers are responsible for opening investigations when readers raise concerns, using appropriate procedures and internal integrity groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Springer Nature reported opening an editorial investigation after reader concerns were raised and consulting its Research Integrity Group. Publishers should act on credible allegations and follow formal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism about citation/metric-only indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: High citation counts or 'highly cited' labels are not alone reliable indicators of research quality and may coexist with multiple retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes researchers with many retractions have still been named 'highly cited'; commenters reference Goodhart's law. Guidance: use qualitative scrutiny in addition to quantitative metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of editorial correction mechanisms (letters/comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should provide and use mechanisms to publish corrections, commentaries, or letters pointing out errors in published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several commenters reported difficulty publishing substantive corrections or letters; one later succeeded after resubmission elsewhere. Best practice: journals should have clear, functional pathways for post-publication correction.
